## PigPhenomics | Applied phenomics and genomics in pigs for the identification and use of new phenotypes in breeding plans

## Research team and collaboration

These research activities were carried out within
the [Animal and Food Genomics Group](https://site.unibo.it/animal-and-food-genomics/en)
at the University of Bologna, led by
[Prof. Luca Fontanesi](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/luca.fontanesi/en).

My contributions are presented within this
collaborative research context.

## Project overview

PigPhenomics investigated the application
of genomic and high-throughput phenotyping
approaches to identify and characterize
novel phenotypes in pigs.

The project combined genomic information
with molecular and phenotypic measurements
to investigate complex traits and explore
their potential applications in animal breeding.

## My research contribution

My research activities focused on the
computational analysis of genomic and
high-throughput metabolomic data to characterize
molecular phenotypes in pigs.

These activities included genome-wide association
studies (GWAS) to investigate genetic factors
affecting metabolite variability, together with
statistical analyses of metabolomic profiles
and the interpretation of genomic regions
associated with molecular traits.

The integration of genomic and metabolomic
information contributed to the characterization
of the genetic architecture of the pig metabolome.
